title: Kuari Pass Trek
reportingPoint: Rishikesh Railway Station. Reporting time: 6:30 AM to 7:30 AM on Day 1. Drop at the same point between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM on Day 6. Please reach Rishikesh a day before.
highlights: Trek to Kuari Pass in the Chamoli district of the Garhwal Himalayas
Walk through the Auli and Gurson meadows
Views of Nanda Devi, Trishul, Chaukhamba, Neelkanth and Dronagiri
Camps at Gulling, Khullara and Tali Top
All 3 meals plus snacks, permits, trekking equipment and a certified trek leader
overview:
Kuari Pass is in the Chamoli district of the Garhwal Himalayas, and the route is also known as the Lord Curzon trail. The trek goes from Joshimath through the Auli and Gurson meadows, oak and deodar forest and snow to the pass. This **5 Nights / 6 Days** trek starts and ends at Rishikesh Railway Station: you need to reach Rishikesh on your own, ideally a day before, and reporting is between 6:30 AM and 7:30 AM on Day 1. Batches run from May to September, with departures every day.

Day 1 is the 300 km drive to Joshimath and a lodge night. Day 2 is a short drive and a 6-7 km trek to Gulling campsite. Day 3 is a 6-7 km trek to Khullara. Day 4 climbs to Kuari Pass and walks down to camp. Day 5 treks down to Dhak and drives to Joshimath, and Day 6 is the drive back to Rishikesh. Transfers, camping, meals, permits, trekking equipment and a trek leader are included. Prices start at ₹9,999 per person (5% GST extra); dual sharing accommodation costs ₹1,000 extra per person.

itinerary.title: Drive to Joshimath (about 300 km)
itinerary.content:
Distance: approximately 300 km. Drive time: about 8 to 9 hours.
Meet at the pickup point by 7:00 AM.
Drive to Joshimath past Devprayag and Rudraprayag, with the Ganga and Alaknanda rivers alongside the road.
Overnight stay in a lodge at Joshimath.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Gulling | Trek
itinerary.content:
Trek distance: about 6-7 km. Trek duration: about 5-6 hours.
After an early breakfast, take a short drive to the start of the trek.
Hike through the green slopes of Gulling and across the Auli meadows.
Pass through the woods, with views of Nanda Devi and other peaks, before the open meadows of Gurson.
Descend through oak, chestnut, deodar and maple trees to the Gulling campsite.
Overnight stay in tents.

itinerary.title: Gulling to Khullara | Trek
itinerary.content:
Trek distance: approximately 6-7 km. Trek duration: approximately 4-5 hours.
After breakfast, start the climb to Khullara through sheep pastures.
From Khullara you can see Chaukhamba, Kedarnath, Neelkanth, Dronagiri, Haathi-Ghodi and other mountains.
Overnight stay in tents.

itinerary.title: Khullara to Kuari Pass and Tali Top | Trek
itinerary.content:
Trek distance: around 7-8 km. Trek duration: around 7-8 hours.
Breakfast at 5:00 AM, then start the climb over steep, rocky terrain towards Kuari Pass.
Walk through deep snow on the way up, with views of Nanda Devi and Trishul.
After time at the pass, walk down to the camp.
If you reach the base camp early, you can trek down to the Tali Top camp.

itinerary.title: Tali Top to Dhak | Drive to Joshimath
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, hike down through small villages and dense thickets to Dhak, on the road that connects Joshimath and the Niti-Malari valley.
Stop at Tugasi and Kharsi to learn about the local culture.
Drive from Dhak to Joshimath.
Hot dinner, a hot shower and an overnight stay in a lodge at Joshimath.

itinerary.title: Joshimath to Rishikesh by road
itinerary.content:
Leave Joshimath at 7:00 AM.
Drive to Rishikesh, where the trek ends.
Drop between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM (timings can change with weather and road conditions).

faqs.q: Where and when does the trek start?
faqs.a: The meeting point is Rishikesh Railway Station. Reporting time is 6:30 AM to 7:30 AM on Day 1, and the drop on Day 6 is between 6:30 PM and 7:30 PM. Timings can change with weather and road conditions.

faqs.q: Do I need to reach Rishikesh on my own?
faqs.a: Yes. You travel to and from the meeting point yourself. Please reach Rishikesh a day before to avoid any delays.

faqs.q: How much does the Kuari Pass Trek cost?
faqs.a: ₹9,999 per person. Dual sharing accommodation is ₹1,000 extra per person, which makes it ₹10,999. 5% GST is extra.

faqs.q: How long are the trek days?
faqs.a: Day 2 is about 6-7 km in 5-6 hours to Gulling. Day 3 is about 6-7 km in 4-5 hours to Khullara. Day 4, the pass day, is around 7-8 km in 7-8 hours and starts with a 5:00 AM breakfast. Day 5 is the walk down to Dhak, followed by the drive to Joshimath.

Pick-up and drop transfers, camping in dome tents (triple sharing) or alpine tents (quad sharing), lodge nights in Joshimath, all 3 meals plus snacks, trekking and forest permits, campsite fees, trekking equipment, a certified trek leader, a trek crew, safety gear and a trek certificate of completion. Trek insurance (₹3,200 per person) and mule offloading (₹500 per day) are not included.

faqs.q: What do I need to carry?
faqs.a: Non-skid, deep-treaded hiking shoes, slippers or sandals, track pants, full-sleeve T-shirts, rainwear, a sun cap, sunscreen and lip balm, a toiletries kit, dry fruits and chocolate bars, a power bank and your personal medicines. Carry a valid government-approved photo ID as well. The full list is under Things To Pack.

faqs.q: How do I book and pay?
faqs.a: Reserve your seat by paying 50% of the trip cost, and pay the rest at least 4 days before the trip. 5% GST is added to the price.

Cancel more than 10 days before the travel date and 50% of the advance is refunded; 5 to 10 days before, 25% of the advance; less than 5 days before, there is no refund. There is no refund for no-shows or early check-outs.
